rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, pretrain_steps=0, n_iter=200, grad_clip=1.0, outer_wall_s=1400, per_scene_s=None, batch_size=1, lr=0.001, optimizer=adam, unet_c=16, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, rationale=iter-2 SIX-BOX. (1) PRIOR: iter-1 hr=0.0 (val_rmse 0.00640 > baseline 0.00521 -> recon WORSE than 128-view sparse FBP), val_ssim=0.940, only 197/200 scans reconstructed because the outer_wall=900s cut the loop at per_scene=4.5s. Ceiling holds. (2) FAILURE MODE: N2I over-smooths -> recon RMSE above the sparse-FBP baseline; ALSO the per-scene budget was so tight (4.5s) that inner N2I steps were wall-clipped well below n_iter=200, so each val scan was UNDER-fit. (3) ONE KNOB: outer_wall_s 900 -> 1400 (per_scene 4.5s -> 7.0s). Everything else identical to iter-1. (4) HYPOTHESIS: giving each per-image N2I fit ~55% more wall lets n_iter=200 actually complete on all 200 scans; if the iter-1 hr=0 was partly under-fitting rather than pure over-smoothing, more inner steps should DROP val_rmse toward/below baseline (hr>0). If hr stays 0 even fully-fit, that is stronger evidence the ceiling is STRUCTURAL (the FBP self-supervision target itself caps N2I), which is the documented finding. (5) BUDGET: warm-start ep=3 (~130s) + 200 scans * 7.0s = 1400s + figure ~= 26 min... TOO LONG for 30-min wall. Correction: keep outer_wall=1400 but it is the WHOLE val-loop cap, and warm-start is separate; 130+1400 = 25.5 min + ~1 min figure = ~26.5 min < 30 min wall. Fits. (6) Loop continues; iter-3 self-dispatched on landing. Reserved levers: n_iter, pretrain_epochs, unet_c, lr, warm_start on/off.
